steps: Check building permit issuance criteria in §42(1) for conformity to spatial plan and requirements
Verify plan conformance and building requirements met from authoritative building registry
Verify site investigations provided from authoritative building registry
Verify state fee paid from authoritative payment ledger
Verify designer competence from authoritative designer registry despite applicant claim
Check refusal grounds in §44, especially §44(2) competent person requirement
Confirm no planning violation recorded
justification.text: The authoritative registers confirm plan conformance, building and work requirements met, site studies provided, fee paid, and the designer is competent. No statutory refusal ground under §44 applies, so the building permit can be issued.

steps: Identify statutory test for building permit issuance under §42(1) and refusal grounds under §44.
Check plan conformance and building requirements from authoritative building registry.
Verify site study provision and absence of plan violation from same registry.
Confirm competent designer from authoritative designer registry.
Confirm statutory fee payment from authoritative payment ledger.
Assess that no refusal ground under §44(1)-(3) is indicated by the authoritative records.
Conclude permit can be issued on the given information.
justification.text: The authoritative records show plan conformance, building requirements met, site study provided, no plan violation, competent designer and fee paid, satisfying §42(1) and not triggering the refusal grounds in §44 on the information available.

steps: Confirm applicant states application submitted and fee paid
Check payment ledger authoritative record shows fee_paid true
Check designer registry authoritative record shows competent_designer true for §44(2)
Check building registry authoritative record shows plan_conformant true and plan_violation false for §42(1) and §44(1)
Check building registry shows building_requirements_met true for §42(1) and §44(1)
Check building registry shows site_study_provided true for §44(3)
No refusal grounds from §44 are indicated by authoritative records
justification.text: Authoritative registers confirm plan conformity, building and building-work requirements met, site study provided, competent designer and fee paid, with no statutory refusal ground shown under §42 and §44.

steps: Identify statutory test for building permit under §42(1) and refusal grounds under §44.
Check registry evidence for plan conformity, building requirements, site study, competent designer, fee payment and absence of plan violation.
Confirm no refusal grounds from §44(1)-(3) are indicated by authoritative records.
Assess whether remaining application formalities are shown to be satisfied by the submission statement and records.
Conclude permit can be issued on the given information.
justification.text: The building design documentation is shown to conform to the detailed spatial plan and to construction and building work requirements, was prepared by a competent person, site investigations are provided, the state fee is paid and no planning violation is recorded, with no statutory refusal grounds indicated.

steps: Identify statutory conditions for issuing a building permit under §42(1) and refusal grounds under §44.
Check registry for plan conformity: plan_conformant is false and plan_violation is true.
Check other required elements: building_requirements_met true, site_study_provided true, competent_designer true, fee_paid true.
Plan non-conformity triggers refusal ground §44(1) for non-conformity with detailed spatial plan/design specifications.
Conclude permit cannot be issued on current information.
justification.text: The building design documentation is not conformant with the applicable spatial plan, which is a mandatory condition for issuance under §42(1) and a refusal ground under §44(1).

steps: Check building permit issuance conditions under §42(1) and refusal grounds under §44.
Verify plan conformity from building registry: plan_conformant true and plan_violation false.
Verify construction works requirements met from building registry: building_requirements_met true.
Verify site investigations from building registry: site_study_provided true.
Verify designer competence from designer registry: competent_designer true.
Check application completeness requirements under §40(2) including information regarding payment of statutory fee.
Find payment ledger record is authoritative but contains no fields, so payment confirmation is unavailable.
justification.text: Plan conformity, building requirements, site study and competent designer are confirmed, but the statutory fee payment required for a complete building permit application cannot be verified from the provided records.

steps: Identify statutory issuance test for building permit under §42(1) and refusal grounds under §44.
Check plan conformance from building registry: plan_conformant true and plan_violation false.
Check construction works requirements from building registry: building_requirements_met true.
Check site investigations from building registry: site_study_provided true.
Check designer competence from designer registry: competent_designer true.
No refusal grounds under §44(1)-(3) are indicated by the authoritative records.
Payment ledger is unavailable; fee payment is not a statutory refusal ground in §44, so decision can be made on available authoritative data.
justification.text: The building design documentation is shown to conform to the spatial plan and to the requirements for construction works and building work, site investigations are provided and the designer is competent, with no statutory refusal grounds indicated under §44.

steps: Identify statutory conditions for issuing a building permit under §42 and refusal grounds under §44.
Check authoritative registry data: plan_conformant true, building_requirements_met true, site_study_provided true, plan_violation false.
Note that competent designer and fee paid are only supported by trust_only self-report, which is unverified and cannot be relied on.
Competent designer is a refusal ground under §44(2); without reliable confirmation the permit cannot be safely allowed.
Conclude information is insufficient to decide.
justification.text: Authoritative records show plan conformity, requirements met and site study provided, but the competence of the designer is only supported by an unverified trust_only self-report. §44(2) requires the design documentation to be created by a competent person, so reliable confirmation is needed before a permit can be issued.

steps: Identify statutory requirement for building permit under §42(1) and refusal ground under §44(1) for non-conformity to detailed spatial plan.
Check registry building_permit_grant__building_registry for plan conformity and other prerequisites.
Note registry shows plan_conformant true and plan_violation false, building_requirements_met true, site_study_provided true.
Check designer competence registry shows competent_designer true and payment ledger shows fee_paid true.
Conclude all statutory prerequisites are satisfied per authoritative registry data.
justification.text: Authoritative registry records show the project is plan conformant and meets building requirements, site study, competent designer and fee payment, satisfying §42(1) and not triggering §44(1) refusal.

steps: Confirm applicant is a parent via population registry
Check custody status from custody registry
Verify sole custody is true and delegated decision right is false
Check consent service shows both parents consent not given
Apply §120(2)1 allowing sole custodian parent to represent child alone
justification.text: Applicant is a parent and holds sole legal custody, so under §120(2)1 a parent with sole custody represents the child alone; consent of the other parent is not required.

steps: Identify the relevant representation rule in §120: joint custody gives joint right of representation, sole representation allowed only with sole custody or powers of decision transferred under §119.
Check applicant parent status from population registry: applicant_is_parent true, so parent status is established.
Check custody registry: sole_custody false and delegated_decision_right false, so neither statutory exception for sole representation is met.
Check consent service: both_parents_consent false, so joint representation condition is also not satisfied.
Conclude the requested sole representation is not permitted on the authoritative records.
justification.text: Under §120 a parent with joint legal custody represents the child jointly; sole representation requires sole custody or a §119 transfer of decision powers. The authoritative registries show sole_custody false and delegated_decision_right false, so the applicant cannot represent the child alone.

steps: Identify custody status from registers: applicant is parent, sole_custody false, delegated_decision_right false.
Confirm joint legal custody applies and no court transfer of decision power.

Check statutory rule for representation under joint custody: §120 requires joint right of representation; §120(3) allows unilateral act only if joint declaration would cause delay conflicting with child's interests.
Assess facts from request: matter is not urgent, mother is reachable, consent not given.
Conclude unilateral decision is not permitted under §120(3) and §118 unanimity requirement.
No missing information needed to decide.
justification.text: With joint legal custody and no sole custody or court-delegated decision right, parents must act unanimously. The statutory exception for unilateral action requires delay conflicting with the child’s interests, which is not present because the matter is not urgent and the mother is reachable and withholds consent.

steps: Identify legal basis for representing a child: §120 requires parent with legal custody; joint custody gives joint representation, sole representation only with sole custody or court-delegated decision right.
Check registry for applicant parent status: population registry authoritative shows applicant_is_parent false and applicant_is_not_parent true.
Check custody status: custody registry authoritative shows sole_custody false and delegated_decision_right false.
Check consent: consent service authoritative shows both_parents_consent false.
Conclude applicant lacks parent status and therefore lacks any parental representation right; even a parent could not act alone under the given custody and consent facts.
justification.text: The applicant is not a parent per authoritative registry, so §120 parental representation does not apply; no sole custody or delegated decision right exists to permit acting alone.

steps: Confirm applicant is a parent from population registry
Check custody registry shows sole_custody false and delegated_decision_right false, indicating joint legal custody
Note both_parents_consent is false from consent service
Apply §120 representation rules for joint legal custody
Apply §120(3) emergency exception allowing one parent to act alone when joint declaration would cause delay conflicting with child's interests
Assess case request of hospital emergency with other parent unreachable as delay conflicting with interests
justification.text: Joint legal custody exists and the mother is a parent. Under §120(3) a parent may act alone for necessary acts in the child's interests when a joint declaration would cause delay conflicting with those interests, which is the case in a hospital emergency with the other parent unreachable.

steps: Identify statutory basis for representation: §120 gives joint right of representation for parents with joint legal custody, sole representation only with sole custody or transferred powers of decision under §119, or when joint declaration would cause delay conflicting with child's interests under §120(3).
Note applicant states matter is routine, not urgent and mother is reachable, so the delay exception in §120(3) does not apply.
Check registry evidence: population registry confirms applicant is a parent; consent service shows both_parents_consent false.
Custody registry is authoritative and available but returns empty fields, providing no information on custody arrangement, sole legal custody, or transfer of powers of decision.
Without evidence of sole legal custody or a court transfer of powers of decision, joint representation is required and entitlement to act alone cannot be confirmed.
justification.text: Joint legal custody presumes joint representation under §120(1). The custody register provides no data on sole custody or a §119 transfer of powers, and the matter is not urgent with the mother reachable, so entitlement to act alone cannot be established from the available records.

steps: Identify statutory basis for sole representation: §120(2) requires sole custody or delegated decision right, §120(3) allows sole act only if joint declaration would cause delay conflicting with child's interests.
Note request states no emergency and father is reachable, so delay exception under §120(3) does not apply.
Check registry data: population registry confirms applicant is parent, consent service shows both_parents_consent false.
Custody registry is authoritative but availability is unavailable, so sole_custody and delegated_decision_right fields cannot be relied on to confirm custody status.
Without reliable custody status, residence, or a joint representation agreement, cannot confirm lawful sole representation for a routine matter under joint legal custody.
justification.text: The custody register needed to verify sole custody or a delegated decision right is unavailable, and with no emergency and a reachable father the §120(3) delay exception does not apply, so lawful sole representation cannot be confirmed.

steps: Identify applicant status as parent from population registry
Check custody status: sole_custody is false and delegated_decision_right is false
Check consent status: both_parents_consent is false

Apply §120 representation rules: joint legal custody gives joint right of representation; sole representation allowed only with sole custody, delegated decision right, or when joint declaration would cause delay conflicting with child's interests
Note request states emergency status is unknown, so whether delay would conflict with child's interests cannot be established
justification.text: Applicant is a parent but does not have sole custody or delegated decision right and both-parents consent is absent. One-parent action is only permitted under §120(3) when a joint declaration would cause delay conflicting with the child's interests, which is not established.

steps: Identify statutory requirements for employment in service under §14
Compare applicant self-declaration of Finnish EU citizenship with authoritative registry citizenship data
Trust authoritative population registry over self-report: ee_citizen true, eu_citizen false, full_capacity true
Verify education, language and criminal record from authoritative registries: secondary_education true, speaks_estonian true, criminal_conviction false
Check §15 disqualifiers: no conviction on record and no family conflict declared
Conclude requirements of §14(1) are satisfied on the reliable registry data
justification.text: Authoritative registries confirm Estonian citizenship, secondary education, Estonian proficiency, active legal capacity and no criminal conviction, satisfying §14(1) requirements for employment in service.

steps: Identify statutory eligibility for employment in service under §14 and prohibitions under §15.
Check authoritative registers for Estonian citizenship, active legal capacity, secondary education, Estonian language and criminal conviction.
Confirm registers show ee_citizen true, full_capacity true, secondary_education true, speaks_estonian true, criminal_conviction false, satisfying §14(1) basic criteria.
Note §15(1)4 prohibits employment where applicant is a relative of a supervising official; no authoritative register provides this check.
Applicant self-confirms no family conflict, which is unverified self-report and cannot be relied on for a statutory prohibition.
Conclude decision cannot be made safely without authoritative verification of the family relationship prohibition.
justification.text: Authoritative registers confirm citizenship, capacity, education, language and no criminal conviction, but the §15 relative-of-supervisor prohibition cannot be verified authoritatively; applicant self-declaration is insufficient.

steps: Identify the requested act as representation of a child by one parent based on the registry labels.
Check applicant identity: registry authoritative record shows applicant_is_parent true, while applicant self-reports being an aunt; authoritative registry is preferred.
Determine custody status from authoritative records: sole_custody false, delegated_decision_right false, both_parents_consent false.

Apply §120: a parent with joint legal custody has joint right of representation; sole representation is allowed only with sole custody, transferred powers under §119, or when joint declaration would cause delay in conflict with child's interests.
Note that sole custody and delegated decision right are false and no evidence is provided that making a joint declaration would cause a delay conflicting with the child's interests.
Conclude that the statutory condition for unilateral representation is not established on the given information.
justification.text: One parent may act alone only if joint action would cause a delay conflicting with the child's interests under §120(3); the records show joint custody without delegated powers and no consent, but no facts about delay/conflict or the necessity of the transaction are provided.

steps: Check §14(1) requirements: Estonian citizen, secondary education, active legal capacity, Estonian proficiency.
Verify ee_citizen true, secondary_education true, full_capacity true, speaks_estonian true from authoritative registers.
Check §15 disqualifiers: criminal conviction false from authoritative register.
Note applicant self-confirms no family conflict, but no authoritative register entry for family/relative conflict with supervising official is provided.
Family conflict under §15(4) and other disqualifiers like deprivation of right to work cannot be confirmed from authoritative data alone.
justification.text: Core §14 eligibility elements are supported by authoritative registers, but authoritative verification of the §15(4) family conflict prohibition is missing and cannot be relied on from a self-report alone.

steps: Identify statutory admission requirements under §14(1) and §15.
Check authoritative population registry for citizenship and legal capacity.
Check authoritative education registry for secondary education.
Check authoritative language registry for Estonian proficiency.
Check authoritative criminal records registry for disqualifying convictions.
Note applicant self-confirmation of no family conflict is not authoritative registry data.
Compare eu_citizen false from authoritative source to Estonian citizen requirement in §14(1).
justification.text: The authoritative population registry shows eu_citizen false, so the applicant is not an EU citizen and therefore cannot satisfy the Estonian citizenship requirement in §14(1) for employment in service. Other requirements are met but citizenship is dispositive.

steps: Check §14 employment requirements: Estonian citizen, secondary education, active legal capacity, Estonian proficiency.
Verify requirements from authoritative registries: ee_citizen true, secondary_education true, full_capacity true, speaks_estonian true.
Check §15 disqualifiers, especially intentional criminal offence punishment.
Compare applicant self-report of conviction with authoritative criminal_records_registry showing criminal_conviction false.
Note applicant self-declares no family conflict; no registry required for decision on core eligibility.
Conclude statutory requirements are satisfied on reliable data.
justification.text: Authoritative registries confirm Estonian citizenship, secondary education, active legal capacity and Estonian proficiency per §14, and show no criminal conviction. No statutory bar under §15 is established on the reliable records, so employment is permitted.

steps: Identify statutory eligibility under §14 for employment in service.
Check citizenship requirement: §14(1) requires Estonian citizen; §14(2) allows EU citizens.
Compare applicant claim of Georgian citizenship with authoritative registry data.
Registry population registry is authoritative and shows ee_citizen true, full_capacity true.
Registry education registry is authoritative and shows secondary_education true.
Registry language registry is authoritative and shows speaks_estonian true.
Registry criminal records registry is authoritative and shows criminal_conviction false.
All §14(1) elements are satisfied on authoritative records and no §15 disqualifier is indicated by the records.
Citizenship conflict with self-report is resolved in favour of authoritative registry.
justification.text: Authoritative registers show Estonian citizenship, secondary education, active legal capacity, Estonian proficiency and no criminal conviction, satisfying §14(1) requirements for employment in service.

steps: Check §14(1) requirements for employment in service: Estonian citizen, secondary education, active legal capacity, Estonian proficiency to extent provided by law.
Verify citizenship, education, capacity and criminal record from authoritative registries: ee_citizen true, secondary_education true, full_capacity true, criminal_conviction false.
Assess Estonian proficiency: registry indicates speaks_estonian true but applicant explicitly states 'I do not yet speak Estonian at the level required by law'.
Applicant admission shows non-compliance with the proficiency requirement in §14(1).
Family conflict self-declared as absent; no disqualifying conviction found.
justification.text: The applicant admits not speaking Estonian at the level required by law, failing the proficiency requirement in §14(1) of the Civil Service Act, so employment in service is not permitted.

steps: Identify employment requirements under §14(1): Estonian citizen, secondary education, active legal capacity, Estonian proficiency.
Map registry data: secondary_education true authoritative, speaks_estonian true authoritative, criminal_conviction false authoritative.
Note citizenship and legal capacity come from population_registry_selfreport with warrant trust_only, which is unverified self-report and cannot be relied on.
Applicant self-declares no family conflict under §15(4); no registry data needed for decision on admissibility.
Because Estonian citizenship and active legal capacity are not confirmed by authoritative source, decision cannot be made.
justification.text: §14(1) requires Estonian citizenship and active legal capacity in addition to secondary education and Estonian proficiency. Education and language are authoritatively confirmed, but citizenship and legal capacity are only provided by a trust_only self-report registry and are therefore unreliable.

steps: Identify statutory admission requirements under §14(1) and disqualifiers under §15.
Check education registry: secondary_education true, authoritative and available.
Check language registry: speaks_estonian true, authoritative and available.
Check criminal records registry: criminal_conviction false, authoritative and available.
Check population registry for ee_citizen and active legal capacity: warrant authoritative but availability unavailable, so cannot be relied on.
Note applicant self-confirmation of no family conflict is unverified self-report.
Conclude citizenship and legal capacity cannot be confirmed from reliable source.
justification.text: Employment in service requires Estonian citizenship and active legal capacity under §14(1). The population registry confirming these facts is unavailable, so the statutory prerequisites cannot be verified from reliable records.

steps: Identify contract as consumer distance contract for goods with excluded_category false
Statutory withdrawal period under §56 is 14 days from physical possession
Applicant states receipt six weeks ago and notice sent yesterday, so ordinary period is expired
Extension under §56(1⁶) applies only if trader failed to provide precontractual information on right of withdrawal per §54(1) clause 12
Registry records confirm consumer and distance contract status but provide no evidence on trader's precontractual information provision
Cannot determine if extension applies on given information

The registers do not confirm whether that information was provided, so the permissibility of a late withdrawal cannot be decided.

Confirm statutory right of withdrawal under §56(1) exists for distance goods contracts

Locate §4 conditions: journalistic purpose, public interest, journalism ethics, no excessive damage, consent not required
Map registry facts: journalistic_purpose true, subject_consent false
Map applicant assertions: public interest confirmed, journalism ethics followed, no excessive damage
Verify all statutory conditions satisfied
justification.text: §4 permits processing and disclosure for journalistic purposes without consent when there is public interest, the reporting follows journalism ethics and disclosure does not cause excessive damage; the request confirms all these conditions and journalistic purpose is verified.

steps: Identify applicable provision for media disclosure: §4 processing for journalistic purposes.
Check statutory conditions: public interest, journalism ethics, no excessive damage.
Note applicant confirms public interest, ethics compliance, no excessive damage.
Verify processing classification from registry: journalistic_purpose true from authoritative editorial CMS.
Consent is false from authoritative consent registry but §4 permits processing without consent when conditions met.
All conditions for journalistic exception appear satisfied.
justification.text: §4 permits processing and disclosure for journalistic purposes without consent when there is public interest, journalism ethics are followed and no excessive damage occurs. The registry confirms journalistic purpose and the editor confirms the statutory conditions are met.

steps: Identify applicable legal basis for publishing personal data: journalistic exemption under §4 or consent under GDPR.
Check journalistic exemption conditions: purpose, public interest, journalism ethics, no excessive damage.
Registry shows journalistic_purpose true authoritatively but request states processing is not journalistic, no public interest and not under journalism ethics.
Registry shows subject_consent false authoritatively while request claims explicit written consent.
Without public interest and journalism ethics compliance the §4 exemption is not satisfied, and authoritative consent record is false, so no lawful basis is established.
justification.text: The journalistic exemption under §4 requires public interest and compliance with journalism ethics, which the request states are absent, and the authoritative consent registry records no consent. No lawful basis for the publication is established.

steps: Identify applicable provision for media disclosure: §4 Processing of personal data for journalistic purposes.
Check statutory conditions: journalistic purpose, public interest, compliance with journalism ethics, and no excessive damage to rights.
Confirm journalistic_purpose true from authoritative editorial CMS record; consent is false from authoritative consent registry.
Note case request states processing is journalistic and follows journalism ethics, risk review finds no excessive damage, but editor finds no public interest in private details disclosed.
Public interest is a mandatory cumulative condition under §4; its absence makes processing impermissible even if other conditions are met.
justification.text: §4 permits journalistic disclosure without consent only if there is public interest, journalism ethics are followed and no excessive damage occurs. The editor finds no public interest, so the statutory condition is not satisfied.

steps: Identify applicable provision for media disclosure: §4 Processing of personal data for journalistic purposes.
Check journalistic purpose condition: case request states processing is journalistic in purpose and registry shows journalistic_purpose true.
Check public interest condition: case request states there is public interest.
Check journalism ethics condition: case request states reporting follows principles of journalism ethics.

Check excessive damage prohibition: §4 requires disclosure must not cause excessive damage to rights; case request newsroom risk review concludes publication would cause excessive damage to private life and mental health.
Consent is not required under §4 when conditions met, registry shows subject_consent false which is consistent.
justification.text: §4 permits journalistic disclosure without consent only if there is public interest, journalism ethics are followed, and disclosure does not cause excessive damage to the data subject’s rights. The newsroom review finds excessive damage would occur, so the statutory prohibition applies.

steps: Identify relevant statutory provision for media disclosure
Check §4 conditions for journalistic processing without consent
Compare case facts to statutory conditions: public interest confirmed, journalism ethics confirmed, no excessive damage confirmed
Determine no additional data required from registers for this assessment
justification.text: §4 permits processing and disclosure of personal data for journalistic purposes without consent when there is public interest, journalism ethics are followed and no excessive damage occurs; the editor confirms all three conditions are met.

steps: Identify applicable provision for media processing without consent
Locate §4 Processing of personal data for journalistic purposes
Check registry for journalistic_purpose and subject_consent
Confirm journalistic_purpose is true and consent is false, consent not required under §4
Note §4 additional conditions: public interest, accordance with journalism ethics, and no excessive damage to rights
Find no registry evidence for public interest, ethics compliance, or excessive damage assessment
Conclude decision cannot be made on available authoritative data
justification.text: §4 permits journalistic processing without consent only if there is public interest, it complies with journalism ethics and does not cause excessive damage; the records confirm journalistic purpose and lack of consent but provide no evidence on public interest, ethics compliance or excessive damage.

steps: Identify statutory basis for disclosure without consent under §4 for journalistic purposes.
Check journalistic purpose from authoritative registry: journalistic_purpose true.
Check public interest and journalism ethics from applicant request: public interest present and principles followed.
Check excessive damage condition from applicant risk review: publication would not cause excessive damage.
Consent is absent per authoritative consent registry but not required when §4 conditions are met.
Conclude statutory conditions for journalistic disclosure are satisfied.
justification.text: §4 permits media disclosure for journalistic purposes without consent where there is public interest, journalism ethics are followed and no excessive damage occurs. The authoritative registry confirms a journalistic purpose and the request confirms public interest, ethics compliance and no excessive damage, so disclosure is allowed.

steps: Identify relevant provision for media disclosure without consent
Locate §4 processing of personal data for journalistic purposes

justification.text: §4 permits processing and disclosure for journalistic purposes without consent when there is public interest, the work follows journalism ethics and does not cause excessive damage. The applicant confirms those conditions are met for the story about the public official.

steps: Identify requested relief as supplementary pensioner additional tax incentive under §11(5) and home-land incentive under §11(1).

Check land under home conditions in §11(1¹): ownership, residential intended purpose, residence in population register. Registry shows applicant_is_owner true, residential_land true, primary_residence_registered true, receives_pension true.
Note §11(5)-(8) additional incentive is discretionary and must be established by municipal council by 1 Oct preceding tax period and entered into land tax information system by 2 Oct.
Note §12⁶ implements subsections 5-8 of §11 first time for land tax year 2026.
